hedges.reason: ETH's measurement window opens on Nov 24, 2025, the same start date as the XPL window, and it resolves on Binance 1-minute highs. ETH is the main large-cap asset that moves with market-wide liquidity. An XPL rally large enough to break the NO legs would need the kind of broad risk-on flow that also carries ETH well above its late-2025 range.

Ethena (ENA) has the same Nov 24, 2025 window and Binance high rules. It is the closest peer to XPL: a stablecoin/synthetic-dollar token that launched on hype and then fell under unlock pressure. A re-rating of stablecoin-chain tokens that lifts XPL through $0.50 or $1.20 would almost certainly lift ENA well above its starting range too, because both depend on growing stablecoin supply and funding-rate-driven speculative demand.

XRP is a large-cap alt tied to payments and stablecoins (RLUSD), and retail piles into it during altcoin seasons. A market-wide alt rally strong enough to multiply XPL several times would very likely push XRP to new highs for the cycle.

claims.reason: For XPL to go from about $0.20 to $1.20 while unlocks are adding supply, capital has to be rotating into alts across the board. That happens in liquidity-driven bull phases, and ETH is the first large-cap to benefit from those flows. A 5x move in a small-cap with heavy unlocks while ETH stays flat does not fit how crypto flows work.

XPL and ENA are priced on the same story: stablecoin growth plus leveraged speculative demand. A re-rating big enough to take XPL back to $1.20 means the stablecoin-token trade is back in fashion, and that trade lifts ENA as well.

A move of more than 2x in XPL to $0.50 from its late-2025 base is most likely to come from a sector-wide rally in stablecoin infrastructure tokens, not something specific to Plasma. ENA has similar beta and the same window, so it would also clear its moderate tier.
